newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MAN CHARGED AFTER GIRL SET ALIGHT
Police in north Queensland have charged a 52-year-old Townsville man with grievous bodily harm and two counts of aggravated assault after he allegedly set alight a 10-year-old girl this evening.
Samantha Green, who suffered second degree burns to her back and arms, is in a satisfactory condition in the Townsville General Hospital.
Police said they were called to an incident at the Townsville suburb of Condon at about 6.30pm.
They said the girl was playing with friends when a man approached the group carrying a container with the top set alight.
The man made some remarks to the children, threw the container away and moved off, police said.
But police said he returned a short time later carrying another container of what is thought to have been methylated spirits, and threw it at the children.
HUNTER VALLEY NEGOTIATIONS BEGIN TODAY
Negotiations between the coal miner's union and Rio Tinto over an enterprise agreement for workers at the Hunter Valley One mine begin again today.
Yesterday 430 striking miners agreed to return to work after a six week strike and enter into a 21 day negotiation period.
The union's Mick Kelly says the negotiations will not be easy, but the union wants to broker an agreement for its workers.
Meanwhile, Mine Manager Allan Davies is pleased the union has agreed to re-enter negotations but says its leadership has crumbled.
Mr Davies says the company is approaching the negotations seriously and will attempt to improve the productivity of the mine.
GOVT TOLD TO DEVELOP INDUSTRY POLICY ASAP
The Federal Government has been warned it needs to develop more vision on where Australian industry is heading, if business is not to become disillusioned.
The call coincides with today's release of the long-awaited Mortimer Report, which has examined the efficiency of government programs, and ways to make business more competitive.
Paul Orton, from the Australian Business Chamber, told ABC Radio the government must develop a full industry policy if it wants to help generate jobs and boost exports.
NAVY VETERANS MAY LOSE ENTITLEMENTS, SAYS ADVOCATE
As many as 10,000 Navy veteranscould lose some of their entitlements to compensation after a change in departmental procedure, a Vietnam vets' advocate said today.
Noel Payne, from the Vietnam Logistical Support Veterans' Association, said naval Vietnam veterans could no longer claim compensation if they were injured outside the war zone in Vietnam.
